description:
Issue summary: During a staged canary fanout for customer ByteWave on a dedicated pool (bw-001) a subset of tenant sessions observed an unexpected, transparent fallback to the stable variant despite an apparent successful prewarm. Impact: ~2% of tenant requests (high-volume customers) saw degraded responses (quality delta) and a token-cost spike as requests were served by the fallback variant and retried. There were intermittent 5xxs reported by the customer.

Impact: Customer-reported quality regressions in production, billing spike for affected requests, and elevated support tickets. No data exfiltration or security issue observed.

Environment: prod us-east, dedicated pool bw-001, orchestrator version v2026.03.09-8a2f, serving-runtime v1.9.4-quant

Steps to reproduce:
1) Configure a weighted canary fanout (10% of traffic) with prewarm-prefetch enabled and a short prewarm window (10s).
2) Start the canary rollout for model open/redwood-rlhf-3b-quant.
3) Simulate network jitter/delay to prewarm agents by throttling control-plane traffic (test harness used during repro).
4) Observe tenant sessions: some are briefly pinned to new variant then responses come from the stable variant with identical session IDs.

Observed logs (representative):
- orchestrator: "fanout: req=canary-227 prewarm_sent nodes=4"
- prewarm-agent: "prefetch: id=abc123 ack_sent latency=130ms"
- edge-proxy: "pin-check: tenant=bytewave session=tx-879 prewarm_state=missing -> triggering fallback"
- serving-runtime: "request: session=tx-879 served_variant=stable-2026-02-28 latency=240ms"

Expected behavior: Tenant session should maintain pin to the canary variant if prewarm completed successfully; fallback should only occur when a node is unhealthy or fails liveness/health checks consistently.

Workarounds applied by Support: 1) Rolled back canary for ByteWave, 2) Re-pinned active sessions to stable, 3) Increased prewarm window to 60s for subsequent rollouts until fix deployed.
comments: Support (Aisha Kaur) 2026-03-10: Customer ByteWave opened an alert reporting mixed-quality responses after we started their canary. They provided session IDs and examples. Reproduced traffic pattern in staging with prewarm throttling.
SRE (Miguel Alvarez) 2026-03-10: Initial triage shows spike in prewarm_ack_latency and several prewarm-agent reconnects. No GPU OOMs. Investigating orchestrator fanout ordering.

Eng (Liam Chen) 2026-03-11: Collected traces across orchestrator -> prewarm -> edge. Found out-of-order processing of prewarm ACKs when fanout concurrent requests overlap; edge sometimes observes 'missing' prewarm state and triggers fallback policy despite later ACK arrival.
Customer (ByteWave - OPS) 2026-03-11: Confirmed rollback reduced quality regressions immediately. Asking for RCA and timeline for fixes; concerned about billing bump.

Eng (Liam Chen) 2026-03-12: Patch merged to orchestrator and edge. Sequence numbers added to prewarm ACKs and cohort commit path waits for stable-prewarm confirmation. Deployed to prod us-east canary, monitored for 24h: no recurrence observed.
Support (Aisha Kaur) 2026-03-12: Notified customer of resolution and billing mitigation offer. Customer accepted rollback credit and will coordinate a follow-up canary with extended prewarm window.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 08:20 UTC - Received alert from CS; initial symptom: mixed variant responses for same session IDs.
Observed metric anomalies: prewarm_ack_latency increased to 200-400ms for affected window; prewarm_ack_loss rate ~0.8%.

Hypothesis: Orchestrator parallel fanout + prewarm ACK race causes edge to evaluate pin state prematurely. When an ACK arrives after edge check, edge treats prewarm as missing and executes fallback path.

Trace evidence: Correlated request timeline shows ACKs arriving out-of-order relative to edge pin-check events. Duplicate ACKs with identical idempotency token observed in logs (possible race in prewarm agent restart path).

Root cause: edge pin-check code assumed monotonic prewarm ACK arrival; orchestrator sent concurrent prewarm requests during fanout and prewarm-agent rejoin produced delayed/duplicate ACKs causing a transient 'missing' state. Fallback policy is sensitive to single missed prewarm ACK during short prewarm windows.
Mitigations tested: increased prewarm window to 60s prevented the symptom; disabling prefetch mirroring also prevented fallback behavior in repro.

Fix implemented: (a) add sequence numbers to prewarm ACKs and require last_ack_seq >= expected_seq before treating prewarm as complete; (b) make cohort commit await a stable-prewarm confirmation; (c) add a short debounce (200ms) before triggering fallback on prewarm missing when recent ACKs are in-flight.
Rollout plan: staged deploy to us-east, monitor prewarm_ack_latency and fallback_rate, then expand globally if stable.
resolution_notes: Patch PRs: github.com/redwood/orchestrator/pull/1225 and github.com/redwood/edge/pull/783 merged 2026-03-12
Hotfix strategy: Canary deploy to prod us-east 2026-03-12 02:00 UTC, monitor 4h, then full deploy 2026-03-12 07:30 UTC.
Outcome: No further transparent fallbacks observed for ByteWave after deploy; fallback_rate for canary fanouts returned to baseline.
Customer remediation: Applied billing credit for affected window; recommended future canaries use 30-60s prewarm depending on pool saturation until additional telemetry rolled out.

Follow-ups: (1) Add dashboard for prewarm_ack sequence gaps and fallback triggers, (2) Update canary runbook to call out prewarm window guidance, (3) Postmortem to be published to Confluence by 2026-03-19.
Post-incident monitoring: Alert 'prefetch_ack_seq_gap' created and set to P2 on recurrence.
